header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Time: 15:00 - 15:52 UTC
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (BlueMarble Lead ML Eng), Tom Reyes (Platform Eng), Marta Silva (Security), Derek Cho (Product)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on model bakeoff results, pinning strategy, and an exercise: simulated rollback drill. Reviewed latest latency/cost tradeoffs; decided to pin to mamba-7b for low-latency endpoints with soft-fallbacks to mamba-13b-q4 for complex prompts. Agreed next steps around benchmarking, pin policy doc, and security validation.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate the time. quick agenda: we want to go over the bakeoff numbers, talk pinning options, and then run a short rollback drill. is that still good?
[00:12] Aisha: yes that's perfect. we had a couple internal questions after the last test run so good timing.
[00:18] Lena: hi all, i'll open with the numbers we collected last week. we ran two main variants: mamba-7b (fp16) and mamba-13b-q4 (4-bit quant). both behind the same routing policy, with prefix/K V cache toggled. note: some logs show "K V cash" in the summary csv so ignore that transcription thing.
[00:34] Lena: raw p95 latency for mamba-7b with prefix cache on was roughly 120ms for our short prompt set, cost per 1M tokens ~ $22 in our bench environment. mamba-13b-q4 p95 was ~260ms with cost ~ $14 per 1M tokens.
[00:52] Tom: wait can you repeat the cost numbers? so 13b-q4 is cheaper?
[00:56] Lena: yes cheaper per token but slower at P95 for the short prompts we care about. longer prompts flip the compute math a bit — the 13b has better throughput on 1k+ token workloads because of kernel packing.
[01:14] Aisha: our user flows are mostly sub-200 token responses for triage and recommendation, so p95 matters more than token unit cost.
[01:22] Samir: that matches what we saw at similar customers — if latency SLO is the priority, we recommend a low-latency model pinned on the route and a fallback set of models for complex, long tails. pinning keeps the model stable during a session and prevents routing jitter.
[01:38] Derek: can you explain "pin" in simple terms? we've seen "pinning" in the console but not the nitty gritty.
[01:44] Lena: sure — pinning attaches a session or user to a specific model version for the duration you choose. it's a config on the route: you can pin by version id or by a version-group. pin means the runtime will favor that model and avoid switching mid-session.
[01:58] Marta: is there an automatic unpin after X minutes? what happens if the pinned model goes unhealthy?
[02:02] Lena: good q. we support TTL-based pin expiry and health checks that trigger a soft fallback. soft fallback is a graceful reroute to a compatible model variant (same schema) and we can run canary traffic to validate.
[02:14] Samir: and importantly, we have an emergency cutoff — if the model fails health probes or p95 spikes above a configured threshold, the routing policy can either: fail closed (return an error), fail open to a cheaper variant, or route to a cached response. you can choose per-route.
[02:28] Aisha: ok that all sounds good. for our SLA, we need sub-200ms p95 for triage. so initial thought was pin mamba-7b on the triage route, fallback to mamba-13b-q4 if capacity constrained. any downsides?
[02:42] Lena: main downside is unit cost — mamba-7b is more expensive in our test harness since it uses bigger GPU burners per qps. also pinning reduces your ability to do automatic capacity hedging across models, because you're locking sessions.
[02:56] Tom: can we do partial pinning? like pin for new sessions only or pin for particular users?
[03:02] Lena: yes you can scope pins by route, by api-key, or user id. you can also combine with autoscale policies that prefer the pinned model but allow burst overflow to a different pool.
[03:12] Samir: ok next i want to run a small tabletop rollback drill. we'll simulate a scenario: at 11am PT a new pin rollout caused a p95 regression on 30% traffic. we need to exercise the runbook. lena, can you run through the steps and i'll roleplay operations?
[03:28] Lena: sure. step 1: detect via the console alert — p95 spikes above 200ms for triage route. step 2: check per-route traces and token-level breakdowns to confirm model is culprit vs infra. remember the console shows token-CPU time and kernel stall metrics.
[03:42] (brief crosstalk)
[03:47] Lena: step 3: if model is culprit, you can either unpin (soft unpin -> allow routing to alternate model) or roll back the deployment (version rollback). soft unpin is faster but can cause user experience variance, rollback is more controlled but requires deployment time.
[04:02] Samir: i'll pretend i'm on-call ops. first thing i do is open the rollback runbook. i see commands for: pin list, unpin session, and emergency rollback endpoint. typing simulated commands now — "redwood rollback --route triage --to-version mamba-7b-v2".
[04:18] Tom: how fast is that rollback? does it drain existing GPU state?
[04:21] Lena: the platform supports warm drain and immediate swap. immediate swap may drop KV cache and warmup cost appears as a short latency bump for a minute or two. warm drain can take longer but smoother.
[04:33] Aisha: we worry about chat sessions losing context if KV is dropped. what's the recommendation?
[04:37] Lena: for session-based flows we recommend soft-fallback first: route to a model variant that has the same KV cache format, or use prefix caching to preserve partial context. if you must swap kernels, plan a blackout window or accept a short degradation and notify users.
[04:52] Marta: from security stance we need audit logs for any rollback action — who ran it, timestamps, and pre/post diffs. does Redwood provide that?
[04:59] Samir: yes, audit trail in the console includes user id, api-key, command, and a snapshot of route config. we can push those logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3.
[05:09] Marta: good. also need to map that to our SOC2 control: change management and emergency changes. we'll send a gap list.
[05:16] Lena: noted. also a doc note: when you plan to rely on soft-fallbacks, add a canary threshold (e.g. 5% traffic for 10m) and circuit-breaker that auto-reverts if error rate increases.
[05:29] Derek: for our tabletop — what's the escalation chain? who is allowed to do emergency rollback?
[05:34] Samir: by default AE/SE can't run rollback in your prod; you'd grant that to your ops roster. we recommend two-person approval for production rollbacks. in the console you can enforce RBAC so only a role can run rollback command.
[05:46] Aisha: ok let's kv-ize that into steps in the runbook. (laughs)
[05:50] (laughs)
[05:53] Lena: next i want to show the bakeoff excel we shared. key columns: p95, p50, tokens/sec, cache hit rate, cost per 1M. the interesting bit: with prefix cache off, mamba-7b p95 jumped to 200ms — so caching gave us a 40% improvement.
[06:12] Tom: what's our cache hit rate on triage prompts?
[06:14] Lena: current hit rate ~ 68% for the sample set. with conservative prompt normalization we think we can push to 75-78%.
[06:22] Aisha: are prompts normalized server side or do we need to change client hashing?
[06:26] Lena: we support both; you can pass normalized prefix or use the runtime's built-in normalizer. we've seen customers change client-side hashing to tune performance.
[06:36] Samir: one more data point: we measured warmup penalty when switching models — approx 30 seconds of elevated p95 while KV warms/compiles. so plan for that in the rollback runbook.
[06:48] Marta: can we snapshot KV before swap and rehydrate after?
[06:51] Lena: partial snapshotting is supported for prefix caches; full KV-state snapshot is more complex and depends on model architecture. mamba line supports prefix snapshot export for sessions.
[07:03] Derek: for the drill, let's simulate an emergency where unpinning did not restore p95. we rolled back to mamba-7b-v1 and still see anomalies — what's next?
[07:13] Lena: next we'd check infra layer: gpu utilization, mem pressure, kernel errors in the node. if infra is congested the fix is capacity burst or autoscale.
[07:22] Samir: also you can route to a different region as fallback. but that introduces latency.
[07:27] Aisha: our compliance team restricts cross-region for PHI data; so region fallback not allowed for triage.
[07:34] Marta: yeah that was the red flag. so for triage we need in-region fallbacks only.
[07:38] Samir: understood, we'll add region constraints to the routing policy for protected routes.
[07:44] Lena: quick note on cost: we can recommend a hybrid pin - pin mamba-7b for 95% of sessions and set a gating rule that moves long-tail requests (>500 tokens) to mamba-13b-q4. that preserves latency for triage but saves cost on long queries.
[07:58] Tom: good idea. can the routing policy inspect token-length and route?
[08:01] Lena: yes, you can add route-level predicates like token_count > 500, prompt_regex, or user_tier.
[08:08] Derek: are those predicates evaluated in the control plane synchronously? any latency impact?
[08:12] Lena: negligible — they're evaluated in the request pipeline before queuing, sub-ms overhead.
[08:17] Aisha: ok practical question: what's the recommended default pin TTL? we don't want sessions pinned forever.
[08:22] Lena: common defaults are 30 minutes for interactive sessions, 24 hours for user-scoped pins. but align with your session semantics.
[08:31] Samir: let's walk through the rollback timeline exercise. we set a detection at t0, ops notified at t0+2m, rollback decision at t0+4m, rollback executed at t0+6m, verification done at t0+10m. that's optimistic but achievable with runbook rehearsed.
[08:47] (typing noises)
[08:50] Marta: is there a way to automate rollback if metrics cross a threshold?
[08:54] Lena: yes, you can wire alerts to an automated policy that triggers auto-unpin or auto-route to fallback. caution: auto actions should be gated with a cooldown.
[09:03] Aisha: can we see the logs that show previous auto actions? did we have any during tests?
[09:08] Lena: in last week’s run we had one auto-fallback event — it's in the audit logs under events: auto-route to mamba-13b-q4 at 2026-09-28T13:12Z due to p95 crossing threshold. i can send that link after call.
[09:20] Samir: action: lena will attach the auto-fallback event to the ticket.
[09:24] (short pause)
[09:27] Derek: switching gears — can we talk about canary plan? we need a safe way to test pin changes.
[09:32] Lena: recommended canary: 5% of traffic for 15 minutes, monitor p95 and err rate. if both within thresholds, ramp to 20% then 50%. use metrics-based gating in console.
[09:43] Tom: ok what's the rollback procedure for canary? is it the same runbook?
[09:46] Lena: same principles — unpin or rollback deployment version. since canary is small, an unpin that routes traffic away is usually sufficient.
[09:53] Aisha: what about warm cache for canary users — do we get cold starts?
[09:58] Lena: canary will see some cold starts; we often prime canary with synthetic traffic to prime KV.
[10:04] Samir: all right real quick — Marta, any security gaps from your side today?
[10:08] Marta: need to see the audit mapping and SSO integration details. also storage encryption at rest for cached snapshots and KMS key policy for the private deployment.
[10:18] Samir: we have SAML SSO docs and KMS integration notes; i'll include them in the doc bundle.
[10:22] Marta: also need to know data retention of logs and whether logs can be redacted for PHI.
[10:29] Lena: logs can be configured to redact PII/PHI fields or to push to a customer-managed S3 encrypted with your KMS. retention policy is configurable per account.
[10:39] Derek: quick tangent — any competitor approaches we should be aware of? we looked at Anthropic and Vertex — Anthropic pushes more model-level safety sandboxes, Vertex had stronger integrated autoscale but vendor lock-in. we like Redwood's unified runtime approach.
[10:56] Samir: thanks. last 10 minutes let's outline the concrete pin decision for next week: proposal is pin mamba-7b for triage route with TTL 30min, fallback to mamba-13b-q4 for token_count >500 and capacity overage, canary process as discussed, and RBAC two-person approve for production rollback. any objections?
[11:13] Aisha: sounds right. need Marta's security signoff before we set prod policy.
[11:18] Marta: yes please send the policy draft and i'll review.
[11:22] Tom: once we get the benchmark logs from lena we'll do an internal smoke test and confirm kpi.
[11:27] Samir: great. i'll send the pin policy and rollback runbook, lena will attach the bench logs and auto-fallback event, and derek will confirm blackout window.
[11:36] (wrap up)
[11:38] Samir: recapping next steps and owners in the doc — any other questions?
[11:41] Aisha: none from me. thanks everyone.
[11:45] Lena: thanks all.
[11:47] Marta: thanks.
[11:50] (call ends, informal chatter for a few seconds)
[52:00] END OF TRANSCRIPT
